text:
ara: Quick thought — rather than special-casing hosted/dedicated/private in a dozen places, what if we model hosting mode as a small finite state machine and converge behaviour through state + capability flags?

matt: Do you mean one SHARED state machine in the control plane, or per-runtime agent?

ara: Per-runtime agent would emit canonical state events, control plane reconciler/routers interpret them. That keeps runtime decisions local but gives a single picture to ops.

sophie: Tradeoffs: simpler global reasoning vs more event plumbing. Also need to handle private (air-gapped) where control plane can't see events.

devon: Proposal sketch: define states {PROVISIONING, ACTIVE, DEGRADED, READONLY, EVICTED} + capabilities like {KV_CACHE, KMS_INTEGRATION, REMOTE_OBS}. Runtime publishes: state, capabilities, last_transition_ts. Control plane routes based on that.

ara: Example transitions I had in mind: PROVISIONING -> ACTIVE | DEGRADED; ACTIVE -> DEGRADED | READONLY | EVICTED; DEGRADED -> ACTIVE | EVICTED.

matt: How would fallback routing work? e.g., hosted receives DEGRADED on a shard and should route to dedicated variant?

devon: Router rules: prefer same-tenant same-mode when ACTIVE. If DEGRADING or DEGRADED, consult capability masks, then fallback order. Fallback policy stays declarative in routing table (per-customer).

sophie: For private/on-prem we need a local reconciler: agent writes events to local audit log and keeps local routing decisions. Control plane may never see them. So API must accept an offline mode.

ara: Agreed. That implies the state model cannot assume central liveness checks — treat control-plane-observed state as _possibly stale_. Add a freshness window and last_heartbeat.

matt: Example config snippet for private mode I'd add to runtime manifest:
```yaml
mode: PRIVATE
state_storage: local
routing_fallback: cached_runtime
capabilities: [KV_CACHE, QUANTIZED_INFERENCE]
```

devon: Telemetry impact: we'll need a small contract for metrics: state_change_count, time_in_state, transition_reasons (short enum). That lets Optimize and Console make sensible suggestions.

sophie: And surface in API: /v1/hosts/<id>/state -> {state, capabilities, last_transition_ts, freshness_ms}. Keep it small and stable.

ara: KMS/HSM differences are tricky — capability flag alone not enough. Need a KMS_compat_level: NONE, INTEGRATED, PROXY. That helps routing and rollout gating.

matt: Edge case: what if a dedicated pool is ACTIVE but lacks a capability (e.g., HSM) and hosted has HSM via proxy? Router needs to compare compat levels and prefer higher compat.

devon: Implementation plan: 1) RFC for state model and capability taxonomy. 2) Adapter shim: emit events to control plane, but degrade gracefully if offline. 3) Router/Console changes to interpret fields. 4) Migrate one small service as pilot.

ara: I'll draft the RFC with the state diagram and capability list. Want to include transition_reason enums like OUT_OF_MEM, KERNEL_PANIC, NETWORK_PARTITION.

matt: I'll help with the router fallback policy examples. Sophie can you sanity-check the API surface?

sophie: Yep, ping me once the draft is up. Also suggest adding a short testplan for offline private cases.

deploy-bot: deploy-check: no CI changes detected; creating RFC draft branch for ara/state-machine-rfc.

matt: Nice — +1 to RFC.

ara: Thanks — aim to ship initial draft by Mon EOD. @sophie @devon please review when available :thumbsup:

sophie: ack

devon: ack
